newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat steady ahead of EU auction results.
newsitem.headline: French wheat steady ahead of EU auction results.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Thursday on hopes that the European Union may again increase subsidies on wheat exports at its weekly grain auction to stay in line with lower world prices.
Wheat into Rouen for November delivery held steady at 840 francs per tonne, dealers said.
Within the EU, the lowest bids for wheat export refunds seemed to have been placed in France, traders said.
Exporters bidding through France have applied for licences to export 706,500 tonnes of free market soft wheat at refunds ranging from 20.47 to 28.89 Ecus per tonne.
In Germany bids to export 34,500 tonnes of free market soft wheat ranged from 21.87 to 22.97 Ecus.
Last week the EU granted 233,700 tonnes of EU free market soft wheat at a refund of 19.98 Ecus per tonne. The award valued late November wheat at some $150 per tonne FOB.
But it carefully avoided covering a sale of 150,000 tonnes of French wheat to Egypt made at $146.50-$147 per tonne, FOB, because of fears of sparking a new wheat subsidy battle with the U.S.
Traders estimated the EU had room to raise its wheat export refund to 22 Ecus without undercutting US wheat prices.
In France traders have offered to export up to 255,000 tonnes of soft wheat with a maximum refund of 22 Ecus per tonne.
Such a refund would value French wheat for late November at around $146 per tonne, FOB.
